disease_label_per_paper: Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis caused by Campylobacter coli in a patient with alcoholic liver cirrhosis
presentation_summary: 46-year-old man with alcoholic liver cirrhosis Child-Pugh class C for three years and type 2 diabetes for about 10 years presented with one day of fever and abdominal pain.
His abdomen was distended with shifting dullness.
Presentation labs included WBC 8,500/uL with neutrophils 86.5%, random glucose 384 mg/dL, creatinine 1.04 mg/dL, total bilirubin 6.60 mg/dL, ALT 27 U/L, ALP 114 U/L, GGT 195 U/L, and CRP 1.9 mg/dL.
Diagnostic paracentesis at presentation showed ascitic WBC 743/uL with 79% neutrophils.
Blood culture organism identification as Campylobacter coli by MALDI-TOF MS and ciprofloxacin response are kept confirmatory/non-ranking.
